trigger: Under GitHub Actions with the manifest psql, a path-1 DSN or job/runner environment whose libpq target differs from the URI authority the loopback check reads: ?host=, ?hostaddr=, ?port=, ?service=, a later '@' (URI or keyword form), or PGHOSTADDR/PGSERVICE set
classification_rationale: The heal's loopback/target bound was decided from the DSN string, not from the server psql actually connected to, contradicting docs/ci-architecture.md:1208-1217 ('never mutates a cluster it cannot prove is disposable') and ensure-postgres.sh:199-200. The facts are the Gate 7 union of the three reports: security-guardian I1 plus I2 (latent: persistent durability-off on a cluster that is not disposable), unhappy-path and consistency-auditor I6(a) false assurance plus I1 and I3; all E4 and verified. The derived HIGH governs over the native labels (security-guardian MEDIUM, unhappy-path high, consistency-auditor medium).
summary: B1 at Gate 7 (security-guardian SG-1, unhappy-path UP-1, consistency-auditor CA-1; none saw the others). pg_dsn_host_port read host:port from the URI authority only, so postgresql://yuzu@127.0.0.1:56551/postgres?port=56552 passed the heal check as 127.0.0.1:56551 while ALTER SYSTEM and the reload landed on :56552 (reproduced on PG 18.6 by the reporters and the orchestrator); ?hostaddr=, ?host= and PGHOSTADDR reached a non-loopback address. Fixed in fda05d5b0 (a plain-URI provability check, refusal when any PGHOST-family variable is set, and an in-session identity guard as the heal session's first statement), then 2365e5187 (the guard failed open on a NULL inet_server_addr(); see cr3-b1) and 551f3ca00 (a path-'@' DSN read as provable; see cr3-new-1). The Gate 8 re-run found SG-1, UP-1 and CA-1 RESOLVED; its residual environment-refusal gap is recorded as sg-r2-2.

trigger: A bespoke path-1 DSN written as password=correct\ horse (keyword form) or ...?pass%77ord=hunter2 (percent-encoded keyword), plus a failed settings read under GitHub Actions
classification_rationale: The read-failed annotation printed a redacted DSN, and the redaction regex misses two shapes libpq accepts, contradicting the change's claim that no new message prints credential material. I1, E4/E5, verified derives HIGH; the native HIGH agrees.
summary: B2 at Gate 7. The read-failed ::error printed (${dsn_redacted}); pg_dsn_redact left 'horse' of a backslash-escaped keyword password, and all of a percent-encoded pass%77ord=hunter2, in clear (reproduced under Actions). Fixed in fda05d5b0: under Actions no new message prints any DSN-derived string beyond host:port, with harness cases for both shapes; 2365e5187 switched harness case 5d to the keyword form so the case discriminates. The Gate 8 re-run found it PARTIAL: the host:port the fix relies on can itself be a password fragment (sg-r2-1). Completed in ce5014f6b (the authority-only parser, so only a parsed host:port or 'host unparsed' is ever printed) and b0f6c4210 (that display form delivered in every message arm, see cr5-f1). Governance r3 re-tested 8 message arms against 6 fragment-shaped DSNs under Actions and found no leak.

trigger: An operator reads the release changelog to learn what changed for their runner, or hits one of the new job-failing arms
classification_rationale: A required doc (the changelog fragment, closed-list item 3) omitted four of the five new job-failing conditions (read failed, settings unreadable, heal failed, still not off after the heal) and scoped the check to 'Every Windows job' when it runs on every path-1 run. I7 with E3, verified, derives MEDIUM; not raised to HIGH because docs/ci-architecture.md:1292-1297 stated every fatal arm. enterprise-readiness ER-1 raised the same omission independently (I7, E3, verified) and proposed the second fragment.
summary: S-1 at Gate 7 (docs-writer D1, enterprise-readiness ER-1). Fixed in fda05d5b0 (the fragment rescoped to path 1 with the fatal arms listed, a second fragment 20260924-ci-weetam-pg-durability-policy.changed.md for the fail-instead-of-fall-back policy, and a matching deploy/windows/README.md sentence) and 2365e5187 (both fragments restate the heal bound and that a manual durability change is reverted by the next job). The Gate 8 re-run found D1 RESOLVED; new fragment wording issues are recorded as dw-n5.

trigger: The yuzu role is not SUPERUSER, allow_alter_system=off, or postgresql.auto.conf is unwritable, locked or on a full disk, and a cluster drifts under GitHub Actions
classification_rationale: The post-read arms withheld the server's own error text although the DSN had already parsed and connected in the same process, so a failed heal could not be diagnosed and the heal only runs under Actions. I5 (that agent's CI lane fails every job until fixed by hand), E4/E5, verified derives MEDIUM. sre SRE-1 reported the same arms independently (I8, E5, verified, LOW); the cluster row takes unhappy-path's band.
summary: S-2 at Gate 7 (unhappy-path UP-2, sre SRE-1). A NOSUPERUSER heal printed only 'psql rc=1 (diagnostic withheld)', hiding 'permission denied to set parameter fsync'. Fixed in fda05d5b0 with one rule: the read arm still withholds raw psql text under Actions; the post-read arms (heal failed, re-read failed) print only server lines starting ERROR/FATAL/WARNING/DETAIL/HINT via p1_server_diag; the final post-heal arm branches on the real outcome. 2365e5187 kept the rc in both post-read prefixes and pinned DETAIL/HINT in the harness. The Gate 8 re-run found UP-2 and SRE-1 RESOLVED; the connection-phase and timeout gaps it found are recorded as sre-6.

trigger: A per-database or per-role synchronous_commit=on, or a -c on the service command line, which ALTER SYSTEM cannot beat
classification_rationale: Every run fails 'still not durability-off 5s after heal', issuing a futile ALTER SYSTEM each time, although a TEMPLATE yuzu_test clone reads off. I5, E4, verified derives MEDIUM. Rejected by a design ruling at Gate 7, not refuted: the reporter's claim that the workload is fast with fsync off and synchronous_commit on was itself marked likely.
summary: S-3 at Gate 7. The proposal was to fail only on fsync or full_page_writes and to warn on a lone synchronous_commit drift. Rejected: provisioning writes all three settings, so 'two of three off' is a state the provisioner never produces and would confound the timing determination the guard exists to make; the fast-workload claim is unmeasured; an override on a disposable CI cluster is a box fault that should fail loudly, and the still-not-off message now names pg_file_settings, the server log and the override to remove. No change; the docs and changelog keep the all-three contract. The Gate 8 re-run recorded UP-3 as ruled out.

trigger: A Wee Tam backend accepts the connection and then stalls on the pg_settings read, a lock, or the ALTER SYSTEM write and fsync of postgresql.auto.conf
classification_rationale: PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT bounds only the connect: the read blocked 23 s behind a relation lock under PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT=10, and the step had no timeout-minutes, so a stall held a runner until the 120-minute job limit, contradicting the Gate 1 claim 'bounded by PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT'. I5, E5, verified derives MEDIUM. build-ci BC-1 raised the same gap independently (I5, E5, likely with the mechanism verified).
summary: S-4 at Gate 7 (unhappy-path UP-5, build-ci BC-1; sre's capacity note also suggested a step timeout). Fixed in fda05d5b0 (p1_psql wrapped in /usr/bin/timeout, an absolute path so MSYS2 never resolves the Windows timeout.exe, and timeout-minutes on the Windows 'Ensure Postgres (server tests)' step) and 2365e5187 (the per-call bound lowered to 30 s and the step raised to 8 minutes, so the script's own worst case, about 341 s, ends inside the step with its own ::error). The Gate 8 re-run found UP-5 and BC-1 RESOLVED; the rc=124 reporting gap is recorded as sre-6 and the timeout pins as bc-5.

trigger: RUNNER_NAME ends in -<n> with n above 2147483647 (10 or more digits) when Assert-Toolchain.ps1 runs with -ExportCiEnv
classification_rationale: [int]$Matches[1] throws under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' and ends the Assert step although the toolchain is healthy, while the bash twin treats the same name as 'not an agent index'. I5, E4, verified derives MEDIUM; the reporter's native NICE disagrees and the derived band governs. E6 not applied: the inventory sentinel reports an unexpected runner name but does not stop it taking a job.
summary: S-5 at Gate 7. pwsh 7.6.6 printed 'Cannot convert value 99999999999 to type System.Int32' and exited 1. Fixed in fda05d5b0: [int]::TryParse with -le 9, plus the consistency-auditor parity pins (ca-5). The Gate 8 re-run found CP-1 RESOLVED: none of -1, -0009, -10, -2147483648, 11- and 20-digit suffixes or a non-ASCII digit threw, and bash agrees on 3.2 and 5.3. A stale comment left by a later restructure is recorded as cp-4.

trigger: A saved but unreloaded pg_hba.conf or postgresql.conf edit on a Wee Tam cluster coinciding with durability drift; agent 0's cluster is also the box-default DSN
classification_rationale: pg_reload_conf() is a cluster-wide SIGHUP, so the heal makes any staged edit live: a staged hba restriction locked out every yuzu client, the message blamed durability, and because Assert runs SELECT 1 against all four clusters on every job the whole Windows pool goes red. I5 (plus I8 for the message), E5, verified derives MEDIUM; not a gating band, so the deferral carries no adjudication record.
summary: S-6 at Gate 7, adapted. The cheap guard was folded in fda05d5b0: the heal session's second statement RAISEs before any ALTER SYSTEM when pg_file_settings has error rows (also closing sre-2's wrong hint), and a failed post-heal re-read is reported as such. The mtime guard that would stop a valid staged pg_hba.conf or pg_ident.conf edit going live (pg_stat_file(...).modification later than pg_conf_load_time()) was deferred: it needs two coincident faults on a disposable box, and its false-positive surface (clock granularity, provisioning order) is a design question. The Gate 8 re-run found UP-4 PARTIAL (a staged pg_hba.conf reject still goes live through the heal's reload, verified) and found the folded guard too broad (sre-5).

trigger: A regression that sends the per-agent heal or re-read to the agent-0 DSN, drops an ALTER or the reload, or makes the per-agent conformance tail fail open (mutants EP-15/15b/16/17/18/22)
classification_rationale: The shipped code was verified correct (I9 today), but the per-agent path had only a happy-path case: EP-18 (heal sent to agent 0's live cluster, exit 0) and EP-22 (fail-open) passed 15/15 on both bashes. A pure I9 reading derives INFO; recorded SHOULD under the severity block's rule that ordinary missing coverage stays SHOULD, as the reporter applied it.
summary: The test obligation attached to B1 at Gate 7. The fake psql kept one global healed marker and matched only 'ALTER SYSTEM SET fsync'. Fixed in fda05d5b0 (runner -1 cases 16-18) and 2365e5187 (the fake keyed by port; the heal call asserted to carry all three ALTERs and pg_reload_conf() to :5434 and nothing to :5433; runner -1 read-fail and unreadable cases; agent-0 case 8b). The Gate 8 re-run found QE-1 RESOLVED; the missing pins on the heal session's own guard text are recorded as qe-n1.

trigger: A path-1 DSN that begins with '-'
classification_rationale: p1_psql passed the conninfo positionally, so a DSN starting with '-' was parsed as psql options: with the heal gate closed, '-cALTER SYSTEM SET work_mem = 77MB' wrote postgresql.auto.conf, contradicting the 'Read-only' comment at :196-197. I9 (whoever sets the DSN already holds the credential), E4, verified derives INFO.

trigger: The last post-heal re-read returns an rc other than 0, or rc 0 with text that is not a pg_settings read
classification_rationale: The final post-heal arm said 'still not durability-off ... re-provision' when the state was never read (I8), and printed rc-0 unparseable text raw under Actions while the fail arm withheld the same text (I9); E5, verified, LOW. security-guardian SG-4 raised the withholding half independently (I9, E4, verified with a fake psql, INFO).
summary: Related to S-2 at Gate 7 (consistency-auditor CA-3, security-guardian SG-4). Fixed in fda05d5b0: the final arm branches on the real last outcome (an rc other than 0 goes to p1_server_diag, rc 0 but unparseable is withheld under Actions, otherwise 'still not off'); 2365e5187 added harness case 20 for the rc-0 unparseable re-read. The Gate 8 re-run found CA-3 and SG-4 RESOLVED.

trigger: YUZU_CI_PG_SLEEP_SCALE=08 or 09
classification_rationale: ^[0-9]+$ admitted 08, and $((2*08)) is an octal arithmetic error that abandons the whole path-1 block and falls through to paths 2-5, bypassing the no-fallback rule and the conformance check (bash 3.2 and 5.3), contradicting the comment that a bad value falls back to 1. I9 because only the selftest sets the seam (to 0); E4, verified, INFO. build-ci BC-3 raised it independently (I9, E4, verified).
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0 (the seam accepts only ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ and otherwise uses 1 with a note); 2365e5187 added harness case 21 for 08. The Gate 8 re-run found SG-5 and BC-3 RESOLVED.

trigger: Agent 0's cluster is briefly unavailable (a restart, crash recovery, or one PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT expiry) when the Ensure Postgres step runs
classification_rationale: Agent 0's first contact was the conformance read with no retry, so it failed in 0 s where agents 1-3 survive the same transient with 1+3 attempts over 6 s; windows-0, the runner under investigation, got the least tolerance. A spurious red job (I8), E5, verified, LOW. consistency-auditor CA-2 raised it independently (I8, E5, verified).
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0: the manifest-vouched SELECT 1 probe with retry became p1_probe_manifest and also runs for the agent-0/base DSN, failing with the same no-fallback error naming the base cluster; 2365e5187 added harness case 8b (4 attempts, rc 1, the agent-0 wording, no DSN). The Gate 8 re-run found BC-2 and CA-2 RESOLVED; the agent-0 message's 'on ?' host is recorded under ca-n3.

trigger: The manifest psql.exe fails to execute under MSYS2 (rc 126 or 127, for example a DLL that fails to load)
classification_rationale: Agents 1-3 reported 'Check the service/orphaned backends' with no rc because the probe discarded its exit code, and comments claimed 'never a broken-psql false positive' and that the -x test catches an MSYS2 exec failure (it checks file mode only). The job still failed loudly (I8), E5, verified, LOW. cross-platform CP-2 raised it independently (I8, E5, verified).
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0 (the probe keeps the last rc; the no-fallback errors print 'psql rc=N' and name 126/127 as 'psql failed to execute') and 2365e5187 (the two overclaiming comments corrected; harness cases 8c/8d pin the 126/127 hints). The Gate 8 re-run found UP-7 and CP-2 RESOLVED; msys2's pinfo.cc maps a missing DLL to 127.

trigger: A parse error in postgresql.conf, followed by any drift
classification_rationale: ALTER SYSTEM succeeded but pg_reload_conf() applied nothing, and the job went red after 5.32 s telling the operator to check pg_settings.source (which reads 'default') and to re-provision (the postmaster then refuses to start); only pg_file_settings explains it. The failure stays visible and diagnosable from the server log, so I8 not I4; E5, verified, LOW.
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0: the heal session's config-parse guard RAISEs before any ALTER SYSTEM when pg_file_settings has error rows; the still-not-off message leads with 'check pg_file_settings and the server log' and never says re-provision; the pre-heal warning no longer asks for re-provisioning; docs/ci-architecture.md mirrors both. The Gate 8 re-run found SRE-2 RESOLVED; the guard's over-broad predicate is recorded as sre-5.

trigger: A drifted cluster, seen from another agent's job
classification_rationale: The fingerprint always printed as a Cyan [info] line and no doc stated the expected values, so 'visible in seconds' held only for a reader who checks every field. I8, E0, likely (the code at :230 does not branch on the values), LOW.
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0 (Yellow '[warn] ... drifted' when any of the three settings is not off, never touching $fail; expected values documented) and 2365e5187 (the classification moved into the exported pure helper Format-YuzuDurabilityFingerprint, with executed contract Checks against real PG 18.6 captures). enterprise-readiness was not re-run at Gate 8; the formatter's remaining pin gaps are recorded under qe-n3.

trigger: Test-ToolchainContract.ps1 run with -AssertPath pointing at a missing file
classification_rationale: The new top-level Resolve-Path/ParseFile ran outside any Check, so the run exited rc 1 after 59 PASS lines with no tally and the other 23 Checks never ran; still red, but harder to diagnose (I9), E4, verified, INFO.
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0: the parse moved inside its Check behind Test-Path. The Gate 8 re-run found QE-3 RESOLVED (a missing -AssertPath now reaches its tally, 76 passed and 10 failed, each FAIL clean).

classification_rationale: Candidate ports 49153-52177 sat inside the Linux and macOS ephemeral ranges, so a 'verified closed' port could open under the check: a spurious red (I8), E5, likely, LOW. The report states no provenance; recorded as introduced because the harness is new in this change.
summary: Fixed in fda05d5b0: five of the six candidates replaced with ports below 32768 outside registered ranges (5433 stays first). The Gate 8 re-run found UP-12 RESOLVED (every candidate port plus 1 is below 32768).

trigger: A regression that drops the TAB, LF or CR flattening or the force flag, or prints raw text in the heal-failed or still-not-off arm (mutants EP-02/03/04/05/07/08/09)
classification_rationale: Case 5's TAB and single-line assertions inspected text that p1_diag withholds under Actions, so they were vacuous, and withholding was observed on 1 of 4 arms. Only the read arm can carry a credential, so I9, E0, verified, INFO.

Fixed in fda05d5b0 (the TAB and single-line checks moved to case 5b and case 2's ::warning:: line; the fake emits an ERROR line plus a non-server sentinel, asserted in cases 6, 6b and 7b) and 2365e5187 (case 2's no-TAB grep had read stderr as a file name and was itself vacuous; cases 12 and 17 assert the read arm's text is withheld). The Gate 8 re-run found it PARTIAL: EP-09 (the CR strip) still survives because no CR-bearing text reaches p1_flatten. Not folded: governance r3 confirmed at 4a7721e13 that EP-09 still survives, the governance r3 fix (ddadfc89f) added no CR-bearing fixture, and the harness at HEAD has none. It was left out for LOC budget under the operator's size exception and goes to the consolidated follow-up issue.

trigger: A heal is attempted while pg_file_settings holds an error row that does not stop a reload: a postmaster parameter changed without a restart ('setting could not be applied'), an invalid value, or such a parameter removed from the files ('cannot be changed without restarting the server')
classification_rationale: The config-parse guard folded for S-6 counts every pg_file_settings error row, so it refuses a heal that would work (without the guard the same ALTERs and reload turned all three settings off, and the server log said 'unaffected changes were applied') and labels a pending restart a parse error. Adjudicated MEDIUM at the Gate 8 disposition with 3 independent reporters: sre SRE-5 (native MEDIUM), unhappy-path N1 (native medium; reproduced on agent 0's exact postgresql.auto.conf layout) and build-ci BC-4, whose native LOW (I8 only) was overruled. security-guardian also noted it as a routed observation (not counted).

Two claims made with that fix were wrong and are recorded as up-r3-n4: the second exclusion string never matches a pg_file_settings row on PG 18.6 (it is the server-log wording), and the documented 'a non-English lc_messages still refuses' caveat is false; the caveat was dropped in ddadfc89f and the predicate kept as a cross-version belt. classification_rationale: Only case 15 exercises the refusal, and only with PGHOST, which does not redirect a URI DSN; the K1 refutation showed that PGHOSTADDR and PGSERVICE are the two that do. trigger: Any failure in the heal step, a hang after connecting that the 30 s wrapper kills, a connection failure after the read, or an operator decoding psql rc 1, 2 or 124 with the documented legend
classification_rationale: Measured on psql 18.6: a failed -c statement under ON_ERROR_STOP=1 (both guard RAISEs, permission errors) exits 1, a malformed DSN exits 2 and the wrapper exits 124, but the legend said 1 = client error or bad DSN and 3 = SQL error, and omitted 124; p1_rc_hint named only 126/127 and the read, heal and re-read arms never called it; p1_server_diag dropped a server FATAL printed inside 'psql: error: connection to server ... failed: FATAL:' (the UP-4 lockout printed 'no ERROR/FATAL/... line'); the harness faked the guard RAISEs as rc 3. The job still fails visibly and the rows' run-it-by-hand steps reach the truth, so I8, E5/E3, verified, LOW. Cluster of 5 reporters at the Gate 8 disposition: sre SRE-6, docs-writer N2, unhappy-path N2 and N3, consistency-auditor N1, build-ci BC-6; security-guardian noted the rc-3 error as a routed observation (not counted).

Test coverage for the 124 hint and the pass-through arms landed in 2e077eda9 (code-review r6), and the docs statements that still contradicted the code were fixed in ddadfc89f (sre-r3-7). classification_rationale: p1_server_diag keeps only lines that start with the English labels, but psql prints them in the server's message language: with lc_messages=de_DE.UTF-8 the annotation lost which guard fired (raw psql showed 'FEHLER:'). The job still fails loudly with its exit code and the guard still fails closed; nothing leaks. I8, E4/E5, verified, LOW.

Fix in ce5014f6b: p1_server_diag also keeps any line containing the guards' own yuzu-heal- RAISE marker, whatever the label language; SET lc_messages='C' is not used because it is superuser-only and would break the documented non-superuser grant. classification_rationale: The environment refusal tests whether each PGHOST-family variable is non-empty, but libpq 18.6 honours PGSERVICE='' and matches a [] section: end to end the log said 'healed on 127.0.0.1:56611' while ALTER SYSTEM landed on another cluster. The in-session guard held its stated bound (loopback plus the DSN's port), so I9, E4, verified, INFO.

classification_rationale: MSYS2 bash upper-cases only a short, fixed list of variable names at startup, so bash sees $PGHOSTADDR as empty while psql.exe's getenv is case-insensitive on Windows and libpq still honours the variable; one defence-in-depth layer is bypassed, and the in-session guard still limits the target to loopback on the DSN's port. I9, E4, likely (from the msys2 source and the Windows documentation, not run on Wee Tam), INFO. The pre-existing PGOPTIONS gate has the same gap.

trigger: The target cluster has a role search_path of 'public, pg_catalog' and a public.inet_server_port() shadow, plus any bypass of the DSN-string checks
classification_rationale: The 'authoritative' identity guard calls inet_server_addr()/inet_server_port() unqualified, so a shadow resolved first through search_path: the guard passed and another cluster was healed while the log claimed :56611; a pg_catalog-qualified guard RAISEd. It needs a pre-planted shadow and a belt bypass, so I9, E4, verified, INFO.

(inet_server_addr, inet_server_port, pg_file_settings, pg_settings, pg_reload_conf). Completed in b0f6c4210 (a SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp as the heal session's first statement, covering string_agg and the inet operators that the qualification did not reach; code-review r5) and ddadfc89f (pg_catalog.string_agg qualified, see qe-r3-7). Governance r3 (security-guardian) planted a public shadow function and showed the search_path pin and the qualification are each independently sufficient.

trigger: A path-1 DSN with a scheme libpq does not treat as a URI (POSTGRESQL://, postgre://, x://), or a ',' multi-host authority
classification_rationale: pg_dsn_target_provable accepts any RFC 3986 scheme in either case and a host class that admits ',', contradicting its own doc comment, the refusal text and the docs table. libpq recognises only postgresql:// and postgres:// (case-sensitive) and takes anything else as a database name on the default target, so a failed read names 127.0.0.1:P although libpq dialled elsewhere (I8); the shape check is looser than documented (I9), but a wrong-cluster mutation cannot occur because the same DSN must pass the read and the identity guard limits any mutation (E6 holds for the I9 part only, so it is not listed). E4, verified, LOW. security-guardian SG-R2-4 raised the scheme half independently (29,040 fuzzed DSNs; every postgres(ql):// disagreement was a libpq parse error).
summary: G2-N4, subsumed by sg-r2-1's authority-only parser: the scheme is anchored to ^postgres(ql):// case-sensitively and ',' is excluded from the host class, with negative fixtures for a non-postgres scheme and a ',' multi-host DSN. Fixed in ce5014f6b; governance r3 (consistency-auditor and security-guardian) checked POSTGRESQL://, PostgreSQL://, postgre://, x:// and comma host lists against libpq and all are refused.

trigger: The toolchain manifest gives a cluster's psql as a JSON array whose first element exists, and Assert-Toolchain.ps1 runs with -ExportCiEnv
